newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee falls on widespread dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee falls on widespread dlr demand.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee fell against the dollar in early Thursday trade, due to commercial and speculative demand for the greenback, dealers said.
At 0510 GMT the rupee was at 58.79 to the dollar, after opening at 58.75 and off a low of 58.86, they said. The rupee closed at 58.72 on Wednesday.
"The rupee opened low and continued to fall to 58.86 on import covering demand, at which level banks sold dollars," said a Hongkong Bank dealer.
The Central Bank pushed up the dollar by 3.25 local cents, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.6253 and 59.8079.
"Speculators are also active as they are banking on continued local demand for dollars and its (the dollar's) overseas gains, especially against the yen," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Overnight call money rates were at 8.75 percent, with the market well offered. The Central Bank's overnight repo rate was at 8.5 percent.
Dealers said low call money rates were also bringing out speculators.
"The dollar rupee exchange rate moving to 59 rupees to the dollar in the coming week is not impossible," said one.
